content.goal: Enable indoor mapping of temperature, humidity, and air quality using a small indoor rover that records measurements with timestamps and associates them with location.
content.problemStatement: Early-stage uncertainty exists around required measurement runtime, spatial resolution, and acceptable accuracy for indoor environmental mapping. The rover must start with a functional architecture that captures data flow and open questions without committing to specific components.
content.intendedContext: A developer or early-stage team will run the rover in an indoor room and review collected measurements and generated summaries to decide next embedded prototype steps.
scope: Functional specification of data acquisition, timestamping, and location association.
Functional design for analysis and basic visualization/summary output.
Explicit identification of unknown measurement and runtime requirements.
outOfScope: Component-part selection (specific sensor modules, MCUs, boards).
PCB layout, schematic validation, simulation execution, and firmware generation.
Regulatory certification, medical-device approval, and production manufacturing planning.
successCriteria: All produced artifacts conform to the v1 contracts.
Explicit and inferred requirements are distinguishable.
Unsupported assumptions are not presented as facts.
The Next Action is derived from concrete blockers and open questions about measurement needs.

assumptions.statement: The initial rover behavior can be evaluated in a single indoor room without needing outdoor mobility constraints.
Early prototypes will tolerate coarse accuracy until runtime, spatial resolution, and measurement quality requirements are confirmed.
